desert_p12_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_001.text: The return path to the grass village was firmer than its first approach had been. Quarry water no longer spread across the low causeway's outer edge, though the displaced central stone remained unsafe for loaded carts. Tuo directed the ridge detour from her seat. The drivers folded the rack before the narrow turn and took each team through separately. Yue stood where the last cart could see the stopping flag, recognising the reed-faced banks. Familiarity made the place less frightening. She kept watching anyway. A remembered clearance did not move the wheel that stood in front of her today.

desert_p12_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_002.text: A white heron rose from the ditch before the leading mule reached it. The bird's legs trailed like dropped reeds, and for a moment its shadow crossed the old wheel ruts without touching either bank. The driver slowed at the turn where their first journey had left the public track. Someone had put two forked branches across the damaged approach. Beneath them hung a scrap of a child's slate, chalked with a cart and a large cross. Gao climbed down to look. The chalk had blurred in yesterday's dew; the branches were freshly cut.

desert_p12_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_003.text: There was someone here who renewed warnings before breakfast. At the drying yard the mat maker greeted them with the relief people show when an expected return becomes actual faces. He noticed Tuo's foot and wisely postponed the dance jokes. Han asked for the collective representatives before unloading the report case. Two women and a young man joined the table, bringing the unanswered quarry letters and a map marked with the spill's edge. Auntie Reed's northern work explained her absence; the others could speak for the present causeway and crop.

desert_p12_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_004.text: Gao laid the new observations beside their existing ones, letting the meeting begin from work the village had already done. The meeting took place under the rack where the mat maker dried long green strips. Sunlight came through the reeds in thin uneven bars. A woman carrying a bowl of bean paste tried to set it on Du's field case, then saw the paper clasp and snatched her bowl back. He moved the case and offered the space. She remained standing, suspicious of a visitor who made himself useful so quickly. Her brother's field lay below the quarry drain.

desert_p12_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_005.text: He had borrowed money for seed, she said, and the first lender's question had been whether the flood counted as weather. She wanted a sentence that would survive that question.

desert_p12_006.speaker: han_xun
desert_p12_006.text: The wind station and lower exchange are separate sites. The proposed freight ground is a buried working roof with present signs of lost support. We recommend keeping loaded carts on the public ridge until a proper structural and downstream drainage inspection. The quarry's temporary berm has helped reduce your lower spill. It also sends water north into an old channel whose farther course needs checking. We have observed new dampness at the exchange. Here are the times, the foreman's work sequence, and the old source reference.

desert_p12_007.speaker: han_xun
desert_p12_007.text: We want your questions in the next proposal before anyone sells a reopening as an easy answer. I can give you the dated instruction that opened the berm, and the clerk's record of when they finished it. I cannot honestly give you a sentence proving how much of your brother's loss came from that work. The channel inspector should come to his field, not make him walk to the office with a handful of mud. I will put that request in the account I submit tomorrow.

desert_p12_008.speaker: han_xun
desert_p12_008.text: If the office asks whether he complained, they can see that he complained here, before the ground had dried and before anyone knew whether his neighbour would complain too.

desert_p12_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_009.text: The villagers read the first page, then asked about crop damage rather than the old case. Gao described what they had seen and what had not been measured. The collective had its own crop account, with quantities of cut grass spoiled and areas still drying safely. Han copied the total only after the representatives agreed the current figures. The report would not turn their estimate into a laboratory result or make it disappear because it came from farmers. Du added the source note in his neat hand. The mat maker watched the attribution more closely than the scholar expected.

desert_p12_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_010.text: The brother arrived halfway through the discussion, still wearing boots crusted with pale earth. He put a seed bag on the table and turned it inside out. Three warped seedlings fell beside the empty bowl. Their roots were short; one green tip persisted, small and stubborn. Nobody tried to call them a representative sample. The man had brought them because he could carry them, because the whole field would not fit into a receiving office. Gao asked permission to draw the roots. He nodded, then asked her to draw the bag as well.

desert_p12_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_011.text: His wife had patched it before the sowing. The repair seemed part of what had been lost. One representative asked why carriers needed the lower exchange at all if its reopening threatened another channel. Han described the distance saving, transfer shelter, and proposed freight service. She listened without agreeing that those benefits outweighed her village's work. A repaired stop might help them sell mats farther north; it might also bring wheels across their fodder route without paying for its wear. She wanted the options compared, including continued use of the public ridge. Gao wrote the alternative explicitly.

desert_p12_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_012.text: The meeting had become a choice about future work, rather than a request for villagers to approve someone else's favourite answer. A carter who bought woven screens from the village wanted the freight ground reopened. He had spent two seasons dragging his goods over the ridge. The woman with the bean paste said the carter's wheels would not lift her brother's crop out of the mud. He said that his work paid for the screens drying above their heads. Both spoke more loudly than the distance between them required. The mat maker reached up and pulled one reed strip loose.

desert_p12_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_013.text: Its end had split where somebody had hurried the bend. She laid it between them. The carter touched the split, then drew his hand back and asked about a trial using empty carts.

desert_p12_014.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p12_014.text: An empty cart can help us inspect the surface under its own load. It cannot give a loaded wagon permission by resemblance. If you want the lower ground reconsidered, we need the drainage inspected first, then the structure, then the approaches. That would cost money and a season of work, perhaps more. I will write a route sketch for the ridge now, with the turns you already use. The question of the lower ground belongs on a different sheet. Otherwise the first tired driver who receives one page will turn a question into a road.

desert_p12_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_015.text: Tuo supplied the route distinctions from her chair. The ridge cost distance but already carried their loaded carts. The foot approach served maintenance and water access, with no implication that freight could follow. The villagers knew parts of those routes under other names. Du kept the local labels beside the formal station terms. Yue watched one woman stop frowning when her family's cutting ground appeared where it belonged. A map that treated the field as blank would have made the next argument harder before anybody reached the room. Its inclusion cost only a little space and the willingness to ask.

desert_p12_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_016.text: Tuo asked the carter about a stone trough east of the reed beds. He said it was still there, though an apricot had grown through the crack. She remembered a road joining the trough from the south. The mat maker's youngest aunt corrected her: the road had once passed west, before the new ditch. Tuo smiled without hiding the mistake. They drew both versions with bits of reed on the dusty table, shifting the old road aside and leaving the new one visible. Yue watched their hands.

desert_p12_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_017.text: A route that had sounded like a confident memory acquired a date and a witness, and grew easier to trust as it grew less grand. Han left copies of the exterior figure, source account, diversion timing, and cooperative meeting request. The collective chose the mat maker and one of the women to carry their questions on the next market wagon to Bitter Wells. They would discuss paid consultation and any continuing maintenance agreement there. Nobody signed away a route or accepted permanent unpaid duties at the drying table. The meeting ended with a practical next journey.

desert_p12_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_018.text: The mat maker fetched bowls while the representatives folded their old letters alongside the new report. Their cracked-bowl correspondence would now travel with something harder for an office to misplace politely. The chosen woman representative had never ridden farther than the weekly market. She asked what clothing people wore when they spoke before the cooperative. Han said she could wear what she wore to the market; the room had benches, not a ceremony. That did not entirely reassure her. Du found a spare folded wrapper and showed her how to cover the papers against grease and rain.

desert_p12_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_019.text: She wrapped them carefully, then unwrapped them to check that the first page was still first. The mat maker said he would carry the wrapper. She told him he could carry their lunch. The whole table laughed, including the man with the ruined seedlings. Yue showed the fish stone to the mat maker's child, who pronounced it more like a sleeping dog. The disagreement amused her after the morning's precise names. Gifts could tolerate interpretations that route instructions could not. She wrapped it again for the shoemaker's girl.

desert_p12_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_020.text: The cook exchanged notes about onion skins with the yard's lunch maker, neither pretending to invent the other person's recipe. Gao bought a small roll of the tougher woven tape Auntie Reed recommended, paid from the field repair allowance. Its use remained a future test, not an immediate guarantee against every wind. Yue helped the child braid a handle for the fish stone. They used a discarded length of rush that had already broken twice under the mat maker's knife. The child wanted to know whether the stone had come from a sea.

desert_p12_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_021.text: Yue said she had found it among other stones and could not tell. The child considered this unsatisfactory, but liked the stone enough to continue. When the handle slipped, he tried a second knot rather than asking her to make it. She had a sudden picture of the shoemaker's girl inspecting the result with a much less charitable eye. The child supplied a second scrap of rush for possible repairs. They left before the afternoon heat strengthened, following the outer track toward the lower plain. The animals worked steadily under their lighter loads.

desert_p12_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_022.text: Tuo rode the rough stretches and walked only short firm portions with Bao's approval, keeping the ankle supported again at each rest. The guide disliked the pace of healing more than the pain itself. Du offered no account of how patience improved character. He simply made room for her staff when she sat. Yue began to recognise that some of the best help never needed to be named in the meeting minutes. Past the reed beds, the ridge widened into an old sheep track. The mules moved more easily there than the drivers did.

desert_p12_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_023.text: One driver kept looking at the grass and asking why anybody would ever choose a road built through salt. The farrier pointed out how fast the grass became mud after hard rain. The driver answered that gravel had its own ways of breaking a man's teeth. Their argument lasted until the cook offered to let them trade places with the leading mule. Neither accepted. Tuo rode with her foot supported on a rolled blanket, listening to the discussion as though the animals had commissioned it for their entertainment.

desert_p12_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_024.text: That evening the water book closed at seven hundred and five litres: three hundred in the first tank, two hundred and thirty in the second, and one hundred and seventy-five in the equipment cart. The day's withdrawals were one hundred and seventy-eight. The first tank still carried the sealed protected compartment. Han read the figures with the drivers while the cook weighed fuel for supper. The return had two ordinary days left on its present schedule. Their margin remained adequate. High cloud gathered again to the north, and Gao marked the change without announcing what it meant.

desert_p12_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_025.text: The evening meal was thick lentil paste with a little onion left from the quarry. The cook scraped the pot clean into the bowls; there was no heroic refusal of supper, only a useful silence while people ate. Gao drew the approaching road under the lantern shade. Han sat beside her and practised the village woman's name until he could say it without looking at the slip. Du repaired the torn corner of his case with the new woven tape. Yue held it steady for him.

desert_p12_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_026.text: He looked at the ugly repair, visibly regretted the old clean corner, and said the case now resembled the people who carried it. Rain reached them the following afternoon as a short hard burst across the low hills. The road darkened, grit turning to slippery paste on exposed stone. Tuo called for the carts to stop at the next wide firm shoulder instead of sheltering beneath an uncertain bank. The drivers moved slowly toward it. Yue held the red flag where wind did not wrap it around her staff.

desert_p12_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_027.text: On the second cart a rear wheel struck a loose slab hidden by runoff. The frame jolted. Its driver braked at once, and the farrier came down beside him before anyone released the team. At first the rain sounded like handfuls of grain thrown against the cart covers. The nearest hill disappeared while the next remained white and sharp. Yue saw runoff searching the roadside dust, making little channels and abandoning them almost at once. Gao signalled the shoulder, but the second cart was already passing the loose slab.

desert_p12_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_028.text: Its wheel climbed, dropped, and struck with a noise Yue felt behind her own ribs. The mule on the inside flinched toward its partner. The driver brought them straight and stopped. For one suspended breath the cart seemed merely embarrassed. Then water struck the road beneath it, clear against the red mud. Water began running beneath the second tank. The impact had damaged the outlet collar, leaving a bright stream against the dark wet frame. Han fetched the repair box while Gao kept people clear of the wheel's unstable side. The driver held the brake.

desert_p12_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_029.text: Bao watched the animals and the people rather than the rushing loss. Yue brought the clean collection pot from the cook, who positioned it under the stream before water struck the ground. The farrier worked from firm stone with the correct wrench. He needed the flow stopped and the cart secured, in that order. The cook seized the clean pot before Yue understood what she was doing. She crouched outside the cart's wheel line and put the mouth directly under the narrow falling stream. The farrier shouted for the pot to stay clear of his hands.

desert_p12_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_030.text: She shifted it without spilling, her shoulders locked against the weight. Water that missed the rim splashed the mud and became impossible to take back. Han stood beside the brake with one hand on the cart rail, keeping the driver from climbing down into the repair space. It was a small crowd around a small failure, every body trying to find a useful place. Yue held the light cover out of the farrier's eyes while he fitted the temporary closing piece from the cart's rated repair kit.

desert_p12_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_031.text: Her palms had healed, but she still avoided taking a loaded rope or forcing the damaged joint with her shoulder. The task required ordinary hands, a clear view, and the tool's known fit. Han steadied the box beside the wheel. The stream thinned, then stopped. Nobody celebrated until the driver checked the brake again and the farrier examined the collar for a renewed drip. Rain ticked against the empty pot lid. The ground had received more water than their margin wanted to spare. Yue's task was to keep the loose cover from whipping across the farrier's face.

desert_p12_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_032.text: She could do it with both elbows low and her feet on ordinary firm ground. The wind wanted the cover badly enough that she had to change her grip twice. The farrier asked for a wedge. A driver passed it from the rated repair box; Yue could see a dark split in the collar where the impact had travelled through the outlet brace. When the closing piece seated, the sound changed from a hard spill to irregular dripping. Nobody cheered. They waited while the farrier watched the seam and asked the cook to move her pot.

desert_p12_033.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p12_033.text: Yue, your right hand is sliding. Fold the edge over the staff and hold the staff instead. There. Keep the cover low. You do not have to make your body heavier to do this. The wedge is taking the closing load; let it. Han, move your boots out of that trickle before the mud takes them. We will all need our feet when the rain finishes. And somebody tell the first driver to keep the leading pair facing forward. They are watching the second cart and inventing their own instructions.

desert_p12_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_034.text: They moved the cart onto the firm shoulder with the tank outlet closed and braced, making no further descent until the farrier checked the temporary repair. Its long-term replacement belonged to the wheelwright in town. The current fix could hold the remaining water and permit a careful return. Gao compared the depth reading with the recorded withdrawals. The tank had lost one hundred and sixty litres before the stream stopped. Eleven had been caught directly in the clean pot. Bao kept that recovered water separate for filtering and boiling after the rain passed.

desert_p12_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_035.text: No one called every caught drop usable merely because it had come from their own tank. When the cart reached the shoulder, rain rattled on its empty cover as though the water still belonged safely inside. The farrier tested the brace against a short controlled draw and found no movement. He had sufficient pieces to stabilize the outlet for the return, not to rebuild its battered mounting. Gao marked the actual break on her sketch of the tank frame. She had inspected the outside tie before departure; the damaged collar lay within a brace that had looked sound.

desert_p12_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_036.text: Her pencil paused over that fact. She wrote it anyway. A drawing that kept her comfortable would tell the workshop less than the broken metal did. The driver sat on the step and stared at the wet road. He said he should have seen the slab. Tuo asked what he actually saw through the runoff. Its edge was submerged; the usual wheel line had looked firm until it shifted. He had braked promptly. The facts did not remove his distress. They kept it from becoming an accusation broader than the event.

desert_p12_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_037.text: Han sat beside him for a minute while the farrier finished. Yue remembered the frightened driver in Bitter Wells and saw the same need now: someone had to let a man begin breathing before asking him to learn from the damage. The driver had been the man most willing to joke about the ridge. Now his mouth kept trying to shape a joke and failing. He looked from the wet wheel to the farrier's hands. Han sat on the opposite cart step, leaving room between them. He asked whether the inside mule had pulled before or after the jolt.

desert_p12_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_038.text: The driver answered, then began to remember the turn, the hidden slab, the moment when braking hard would have put both animals sideways. Han listened without interrupting. The account gave the driver something to do besides punish himself with the sound of running water.

desert_p12_039.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p12_039.text: Drink your allotted water. You have been holding yourself rigid since the jolt, and that will not put a litre back. Nobody is taking your cup to repair the account. Tell me whether you struck your knee or twisted anything when you braked. Here? Only bruised, apparently. We shall watch it. The animals are sound, the cart is secure, and the temporary closure is being checked. We have enough water to finish the immediate journey, including the emergency reserve if needed. That last part is why it travelled with us. It was not packed to admire its unbroken red thread.

desert_p12_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_040.text: The driver drank, looking ashamed of how much the ordinary act helped. Bao checked his knee, then Tuo's ankle after the rough ride. The guide had no new concerning change, though both would need gentler pacing tomorrow. The mules had avoided injury; the farrier examined their feet on firm gravel after the rain eased. Plum snorted at the wet harness and turned toward her driver. Its annoyance sounded reassuringly normal. Yue helped lay the damp shade cloth where it could drain without dripping into the food bags. Their camp would be simpler tonight, with every unnecessary lift deferred.

desert_p12_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_041.text: The rain moved off before sunset. A narrow yellow bar opened between two clouds and lit the wet gravel so brightly that every hollow looked filled with metal. The farrier washed his cut knuckle with the day's medical allowance and let Bao cover it. Yue's hands were red from the cover's rough edge but unbroken; Bao told her to leave the wrapping work to somebody else that evening. Tuo made the driver turn his knee both ways while she watched. He asked whether every person in camp intended to inspect him.

desert_p12_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_042.text: She said he was free to inspect her ankle after the clinician finished with it. The cook filtered and boiled the eleven recovered litres in the small kettle, using an additional measured kilogram of charcoal. Ten clean litres survived cooling and transfer into the first tank. The remaining litre belonged to treatment and handling loss. Gao entered the actual recovery against the tank's one hundred and sixty-litre drop, leaving a net loss of one hundred and fifty. The arithmetic felt brutal because every term had a sound and movement attached to it.

desert_p12_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_043.text: Han checked the entries, then gave the page to the drivers. A truthful smaller total was more useful than a hopeful recovered jar left unmeasured beside the stove. Boiling the recovered water took longer than anybody wished. The cook watched the small kettle and kept the lid seated. The stove stood on flat stones above the wet shoulder, its smoke falling sideways before rising. A mule nosed at the wood of the first cart and found nothing edible. Yue counted the cooling vessel once with Gao and once with the cook, then stopped counting.

desert_p12_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_044.text: Ten litres looked absurdly small beside the muddy trace left by the lost water. It also looked like ten litres. The cook lowered the last cup into the first tank and wiped the clean rim with a separate cloth. After the day's one hundred and eighty-eight litres withdrawn and the net leak loss, three hundred and sixty-seven remained. The first tank held two hundred and fifty, including its protected two hundred; the second held twelve; the equipment cart held one hundred and five. Routine water above the protected amount totalled one hundred and sixty-seven. Tomorrow's actual need could exceed that.

desert_p12_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_045.text: Han opened the return plan and removed every optional stop. They would still rest when bodies and animals required. The missing litre against the ordinary forecast was a reason to use the reserve honestly, not a command to make thirst obey a figure.

desert_p12_046.speaker: han_xun
desert_p12_046.text: Tomorrow we use the protected compartment if we need it. The seal is there so that we know when and why it is opened. I will not have any of you hiding thirst because you think a clean seal will make the report better. Tell Bao if you feel wrong, tell the driver if the pace is wrong, and tell me if you hear somebody offering to drink less to pay for this. The workshop can argue about metal when we are home. Our job tonight is to arrive there with people and animals who can stand in the yard.

desert_p12_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_047.text: Gao checked the public route ahead with Tuo's seated account and the drivers' observed ground. Bitter Wells remained within the next day's safe ordinary travel, provided they kept the repaired cart slow at rough places. The road did not require crossing the flooded culvert; their outer detour remained available. Turning back toward the quarry would lengthen the journey and offer no promised surplus water. Continuing toward town was the stronger option. Du packed the report case where it could not be struck by shifting tools.

desert_p12_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_048.text: The evidence would travel with the people, not compete with them for a reckless extra mile. The nearer town route followed a broad black gravel tongue between two shallow washes. Tuo remembered a stand of orchard willows beyond the final turn; the drivers had seen those same willows on their outward journey. Gao asked each man separately about the intervening ground. Their distances differed a little, their turns did not. The longer quarry return would lead them away from the town without a promise of sale water at its end.

desert_p12_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_049.text: The choice felt almost offensively plain after so much lost water. Yue wanted an ingenious route to appear on Du's map. He closed the folder and said they had a good enough route already. That night the driver with the wooden bird played no tune. He checked his daughter's gift for dampness and held it quietly against his knee. Long Legs sat beside him without a joke, helping clean grit from the damaged cart's outer fittings. Han wrote the failure record while Gao supplied the measurements. Bao prepared the morning care portions.

desert_p12_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_050.text: Tuo stared at the rain-cleared sky and said the weather had not meant anything personal by arriving. Nobody contradicted her. Yue found the sentence comforting precisely because it did not ask the driver to feel better on command. The wooden bird lay on the driver's knee, its painted wing darkened by a drop of rain. He turned it toward the lantern and found the paint intact. Yue asked whether his daughter knew what species it was meant to be. He said she had ordered a bird that could live in a house without dropping feathers on the quilts.

desert_p12_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_051.text: His wife had voted for the wooden one. The story eventually drew a smile from him. He put the bird into the dry inner pocket of his coat and slept leaning against the wheel, his boot still where he could feel any movement of the brake. The last morning began cool. The crew ate before moving, and the farrier checked the temporary collar under a small test draw. It remained dry where the brace held. The twelve litres in the second tank would be used through the repaired outlet carefully rather than left to become a reassuring inaccessible number.

desert_p12_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_052.text: Tuo rode the first stretch, directing the return turn from the shaded seat. Bao walked where the cart jolts became strongest. Yue held the flag at each narrowed sightline. The road had become familiar enough to demand fewer guesses, and still required attention at every wet patch. Morning gave them a low pale sun and air cool enough to make the cook reluctant to leave the stove. Breakfast came out in smaller bowls because the bowls packed more easily; the portions themselves were unchanged. Han walked the six mules with the farrier while the drivers checked their harness.

desert_p12_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_053.text: The animal that had flinched at the jolt stretched its neck into the man's sleeve and allowed the examination. Tuo watched from the passenger place, impatient with her supported foot and grateful for it in equal measure. Yue shook the sand from the cloak and folded the side that had covered the farrier's eyes inward. Near the lower plain the first tank's routine compartment reached its planned last draw. Han cut the red seal and measured five litres from the protected supply for the day's necessary portions.

desert_p12_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_054.text: He wrote the reason and volume immediately, then passed the vessel to Bao for distribution with the existing care plan. The thread no longer remained whole. The people and animals remained properly watered. The reserve had served the purpose named when they loaded it, without becoming an excuse to extend the survey or suppress anyone's need. Yue watched the red scrap enter the account pouch beside the failure note. The red thread made a tiny sound when Han cut it. Yue had heard louder sounds from dry grass.

desert_p12_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_055.text: He tied the cut ends to the account slip rather than throw them away, then measured the necessary five litres into the working vessel. The driver watched the level with a hunger for numbers that was not entirely about thirst. Han gave him the next cup to carry to the cook. The ordinary task steadied his hands. Yue saw the protected compartment's remaining line settle below the old mark. The mark stayed visible, an honest witness to both the precaution and the day when the precaution was used.

desert_p12_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_056.text: They reached the final dark stretch before town while the afternoon light remained manageable. Treadle wheels moved in the orchard plots, carrying municipal water into green channels. Yue could hear their creak before seeing the gate. The sound made the last mile feel both shorter and strangely difficult: her body had begun believing in rest and wanted it immediately. Gao walked beside her until the wheel line widened. Neither spoke much. The borrowed staff had helped through many miles. Now its cap struck familiar harder paving, and Yue felt the basin dust changing beneath her sandals.

desert_p12_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_057.text: A boy driving an orchard donkey met them beside the first treadle wheel. He had a basket of split apricots and wanted to sell them before he went home. The cook bought enough for the crew from her own meal purse and asked him whether the gate road was open. He pointed with a sticky finger, describing the scaffold everyone in town had been cursing for a week. His donkey tried to eat a cart tassel. The second driver laughed for the first time since the break and gently moved the tassel out of reach.

desert_p12_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_058.text: Juice ran down Yue's wrist when she bit an apricot. She held it over the dust and let herself enjoy it. The Black Gate's western scaffolding still stood, though the eastern jamb had been repaired neatly. The watchman recognised the three carts and called the mason's clearance across the passage. Tuo sat upright to direct the narrow entry, allowing no wave of homecoming to replace the known wheel drop. Long Legs brought the first pair through straight. The second driver followed at the slower pace its repair required. The equipment cart passed last with Bao watching the supported ankle.

desert_p12_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_059.text: Han counted the animals on the town side. All six were there. All twelve people were there. The report case stayed closed until the carts stood safely. The gate mason recognized Han before he recognized the caravan. He asked whether the north road still stole wheels. Han said the north road had tried for water this time. The mason's smile faded at the patched outlet, and he put down his trowel to guide the leading cart between two piles of new stone.

desert_p12_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_060.text: Town noise came through the opening: a bell from a bean shop, a woman calling for a missing account book, somebody practising the same four notes on a flute. Yue had imagined arrival as a clean sudden release. Instead it happened one axle at a time, amid people whose day had already begun. At the yard they drank from the separate municipal supply before anybody began unloading heavy work. The caravan tanks ended with one hundred and ninety-five litres, all remaining in the first tank's protected compartment. The last day's actual withdrawals had totalled one hundred and seventy-two.

desert_p12_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_061.text: The temporary collar held through the journey. Han read the closing amount, then handed the repair record to the wheelwright instead of calling the safe arrival proof that the joint needed no replacement. Bao directed Tuo and the bruised driver toward the clinic's afternoon examination. Arrival completed the road, not every consequence it had carried. The yard keeper brought cups without waiting to be asked. The first driver drank, handed his cup back, and stood with both palms against the gatepost.

desert_p12_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_062.text: The farrier led the mules to the established trough, where the keeper checked that the water was running clean from the town service. The crew's travelling stock stood untouched while people recovered their breath. Gao kept her field case on the high bench away from the washing splash. When the keeper asked whether the expedition had found the lost palace, she said they had found a store with a name, a road with a warning, and two men who wanted to be home. He decided this was a better result.

desert_p12_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_063.text: Han's daughter came through the yard gate with a four-wheeled cart drawing held above her head. Its enormous flower now occupied the whole side. The drivers demanded royalties for the idea. She lowered the paper when she saw Tuo's foot and the damaged collar, then looked at her father with a seriousness that made him stop smiling. He said everyone had returned and the clinic would check the injuries. She nodded, walked over, and embraced him before asking about the accounts. For a little while he stood with his face against her hair, no factor's answer available or required.

desert_p12_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_064.text: Han's daughter called the drawing a redesign. The enormous flower was a loading canopy, she explained, and the fourth wheel was there because her father always complained about balance. He asked where a driver would sit. She made a small fierce circle beside the flower and said he could sit wherever he liked once he remembered to come home. Han laughed, then caught her hand and held it a little too long. She let him. The receiving clerk looked away toward the empty yard, granting them a private patch of ground without pretending that work had stopped.

desert_p12_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_065.text: Yue took the fish stone to the shoemaker's stall before the shutters closed. The girl accepted it, turned it over, and decided it was a fish dreaming of becoming a dog. Yue said two other judges had reached similar conclusions. The child placed it beside her coin tin with perfect satisfaction. No further proof was needed. The shoemaker inspected Yue's altered sandal strap, asked whether it held, and looked pleased when she said yes.

desert_p12_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_066.text: She bought a small repair for the worn sole, paying from her wages already earned, and let the ordinary exchange bring the first journey to a quiet point. The shoemaker's girl sat the stone on the counter beside a row of unpaired heels. She tried the rush handle, declared the knot interesting, and untied it. Her own knot held after a sharp pull. Yue surrendered the spare rush to her without argument. The girl asked whether salt made a desert white like flour. Yue described the hard crust, the red gravel beside it, the sudden green of the village.

desert_p12_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_067.text: The girl listened while her father put a new sole against Yue's boot. When the hammer began, she arranged the stone among the heels as if it were a visiting customer waiting its turn. At the clinic Bao handed over the return injury notes and asked for the guides' current room. The patient wagon had arrived safely earlier that day. The younger guide had received fuller examination and proper continuing support for the injured leg; recovery would take time. Her mother had brought the warm blue shawl. The older guide rested nearby, still tired but no longer stranded.

desert_p12_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_068.text: Yue saw them briefly with their consent, bringing no public report to the bedside. The woman recognised her and asked whether the carts had behaved on the way home. Yue said one required a serious conversation with the wheelwright. The younger guide's room smelled of broth and clean linen. Her mother had put the requested blue shawl over the chair, where she could see it without being too warm. She recognized Yue, then frowned as though recognizing someone from the accident might bring the accident back into the room.

desert_p12_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_069.text: Yue said the handcart remained with the quarry keeper under the guides' names. The woman asked for her own field notebook, brought from home by her mother and lying on the bedside table, with the water glass on a separate board. Yue stayed briefly to say the older guide was asking after her; the clinician wanted her to sleep. The woman laughed, then grew quiet as she heard the account of everyone returning. She wanted the notebook after supper so she could correct the shelf route while the memory remained clear.

desert_p12_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_070.text: Bao told her to rest between the pages. Her mother thanked Yue and the crew without asking the scene to become a formal ceremony. The shawl lay across the blanket, blue and warm-looking even in the shaded room. Yue had helped hold a bag beside a stretcher. Here that small role found its consequence in a person who could joke, recover, and decide how to tell her own story. Outside the room, the mother told Bao that she had spent the first evening angry with every person who came through the door.

desert_p12_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_071.text: The clinician had been sensible enough not to tell her to be grateful. Bao said gratitude was a poor substitute for rest, then helped her fold the shawl's hanging fringe away from the basin. The mother laughed again, more easily. Yue waited by the passage window, looking at the slate roofs beyond it. She thought of the bordered cloth at the mast and of Tuo's brother's winter return. This mother had a living daughter in the next room. The fact needed no lesson attached to it.

desert_p12_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_072.text: Han settled the immediate wages at the receiving counter, including waiting days and the extra carrying entries. The deposited return fund remained separate until its keeper confirmed no crew claim outstanding; its release would follow the actual accounts. Gao retained the original field case for the cooperative meeting. Du returned to the workers' room with the source-copy bundle protected beneath a proper padded lid. Tuo went home with instructions to keep the ankle rested, grumbling more softly now that a clinician had repeated Bao's judgement. The town received each of them into different obligations. The report would have to follow.

desert_p12_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_073.text: The wages made a subdued little music as the counter clerk laid out the coins. The driver who had held the second cart asked whether the collar loss would come out of his share. Han pushed the full agreed sum toward him and said the workshop investigation came first; the driver's pay was not a receptacle for every unexplained loss. The driver covered the coins with his hand. Beyond him, the cook argued cheerfully for the cost of the apricots, then admitted they had been her own gift and withdrew the claim.

desert_p12_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_074.text: Yue collected her pay and put half aside before the tempting smells from the street could persuade her otherwise. That evening Yue washed the issued cloak and hung it where the shopkeeper's daughter had once left her beetle sums. She sat beside the open window with the private notebook, too tired to make the return sound grand. She wrote that they had drawn from the protected water because bodies needed it. She wrote that the glass case remained at the exchange, and that the village still maintained the tap. Then she stopped.

desert_p12_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_075.text: Below, a child argued that her stone was definitely a fish. The familiar street held a room for what the desert had changed, without needing to resemble it. The shopkeeper's daughter came up to the roof carrying an empty basket. She asked why the cloak looked as though somebody had tried to mop a river with it. Yue described the rain in a few sentences. The girl inspected the roughened edge and offered a needle. They sat beneath the washing line while the town cooled around them. The first stitch went crooked; the second found the old weave.

desert_p12_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p12_076.text: Below, a neighbour quarrelled with a cat over a piece of dried fish. Yue let the familiar noise fill the spaces between her account of the road, until she could feel how tired she was and go to bed.
